1.explanation: The TableSelectRow component is responsible for rendering the <td> cell that wraps the InlineCheckbox or RadioButton, but its implementation only uses the incoming `className` prop and does not append the default `bx--table-column-checkbox` class. The getSelectionProps method in DataTable should supply a `className` that includes the Carbon prefix, but because TableSelectRow doesn’t merge it with its own default styling, the cell ends up unstyled. Fixing TableSelectRow to merge its default `bx--table-column-checkbox` class with any passed-in className (for example `<td className={`${className} bx--table-column-checkbox`}>`) restores the correct 48px row height and expected styling.
1.bug_scenario: When rendering a selectable DataTable in React, the <td> wrapper around the row-selection checkbox is missing the Carbon class `bx--table-column-checkbox`. On the official Carbon site this class adds 48px row height, but in React the missing class yields a 52px height and misaligned styling. The screenshots show that the `<td>` generated by TableSelectRow has no `bx--table-column-checkbox` class.

2.explanation: 1. TableSelectRow: This component renders the <td> around each inline checkbox. Currently it does `<td className={className}>` without ever adding the mandatory `bx--table-column-checkbox` class, so the styles that set row height and padding are missing. 2. DataTable.getSelectionProps: This prop-getter supplies the props passed into TableSelectRow (including className). It never injects the table-column-checkbox classname for rows, so TableSelectRow never receives it. Fixing either by hardcoding the prefix class in TableSelectRow or by having getSelectionProps include it will restore the correct styling and row height.
2.bug_scenario: When rendering a selectable DataTable in React, the <td> cell wrapping each row’s checkbox is missing the “bx--table-column-checkbox” class. As a result, row-height and styling don’t match vanilla Carbon (rows render at 52px high instead of 48px). The screenshots show that the header <th> has the correct class, but each row’s <td> has no class at all, so the CSS isn’t applied.
